title: Autonomic reflexes
objective: Explain an autonomic reflex arc using the baroreflex as an example.

steps.title: Reflexes you don't command
steps.body: **[[autonomic nervous system|Autonomic]]** reflexes keep organs in check without conscious control. In the **[[baroreflex]]**, stretch receptors in big arteries sense blood pressure; the brainstem responds via **[[sympathetic]]** and **[[parasympathetic]]** (**[[vagus]]**) output to adjust heart rate and vessel tone — a negative-feedback arc for pressure.

steps.prompt: Blood pressure suddenly rises. In the baroreflex, what happens?
options: Baroreceptors fire more; the vagus slows the heart
Baroreceptors fire less; sympathetic drive speeds the heart
Baroreceptors fire more; sympathetic drive slows the heart
Baroreceptors fire more; the vagus speeds the heart up
steps.explanation: Higher pressure stretches baroreceptors more; parasympathetic (vagal) output slows the heart and sympathetic tone drops, lowering pressure — negative feedback.

variants.setup: Arterial pressure spikes and baroreceptors fire harder.
options: Slow the heart and lower pressure
Speed the heart and raise pressure
variants.reveal: The baroreflex opposes the rise: it slows the heart and drops pressure.

steps.setup: You stand up quickly and blood pressure briefly drops.
steps.prompt: What do you predict the baroreflex does?
options: Raises heart rate and vessel tone to restore pressure
Lowers heart rate to ease the strain on the heart
Nothing at all, since it only senses high pressure
steps.reveal: Falling pressure means less baroreceptor firing; the reflex raises sympathetic output (faster heart, tighter vessels) to bring pressure back — the same arc, opposite direction.

variants.prompt: On standing, a pressure drop triggers the baroreflex to…
options: Raise both the heart rate and the vessel tone
Slow the heart to ease its workload
Nothing, since baroreceptors sense only high pressure
variants.explanation: Less baroreceptor firing drives sympathetic output up to restore pressure.

steps.title: The afferent limb is interoceptive
steps.body: The baroreflex's sensory limb is an [[interoception|interoceptive]] afferent — the nervous system reading an internal variable. Visceral afferents (the lab's focus) are the afferent limb of many such organ reflexes.

reviewNotes: Baroreflex as autonomic negative feedback; interoceptive afferent limb.
